claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy with a uniform microstructure.
Increasing Cr and/or Al concentration in CoCrFeMnNi enhances formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
Increasing Cr and/or Al concentration improves retention and adherence of the protective oxide scale.
Cr and Al provide a high thermodynamic driving force for Cr2O3 and Al2O3 formation.
Cr2O3, Al2O3, or mixed oxides can constitute the protective surface scale.
High-entropy alloy matrices possess inherently sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish matrix diffusion promotes self-healing of the oxide scale.
A continuous protective oxide scale limits inward oxygen transport and further oxidation.
Alloys with increased Cr and/or Al will develop thinner oxide scales than the lower-Cr/Al baseline.
Alloys with increased Cr and/or Al will develop more continuous and slower-growing oxide scales than the baseline.
Alloys with increased Cr and/or Al will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than the baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate at approximately 1000°C under controlled oxygen partial pressures.
Changing the temperature substantially may produce alternative oxidation behavior.
Mixed oxide phases may complicate the oxidation behavior.
Diffusion kinetics may deviate from the proposed sluggish-diffusion behavior.
The comparison should expose high- and low-Cr/Al alloy series to identical 1000°C oxidation conditions for 200 hours.
The hypothesis is falsified if increased-Cr/Al alloys fail to show thinner, more continuous, slower-growing scales and lower weight gain, or if diffusion is not slower.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes the alloys as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi while the intervention varies Cr and/or adds Al with the other elements held constant. Those modified alloys cannot all remain equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, and Al-containing variants are no longer five-component CoCrFeMnNi alloys.

The initial state includes systematic Cr/Al variations, whereas the baseline is separately described as equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi with low Cr/Al. The reference composition and meaning of 'low' are not consistently defined; equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi contains 20 at.% Cr and no Al.
